title: Functions
summary: Declare functions with typed parameters and return types, and see what scope means.

blocks.html:
A function is a named piece of work you call by name as often as you like. PHP ships with thousands of them — count(), strlen(), number_format() — and you declare your own with one keyword.

Here is isEven() from example.php in this project. Read the signature twice: it takes an int and promises a bool.

blocks.title: isEven() from example.php
blocks.code:
<?php

function isEven(int $number): bool
{
    return $number % 2 === 0;
}

foreach ([7, 8] as $num) {
    echo $num, ' is even: ', (isEven($num) ? 'true' : 'false'), "\n";
}
blocks.output:
7 is even: false
8 is even: true

blocks.html:
function names it. int $number is a parameter with a type. : bool is the return type. PHP checks both: hand the function something that is not an integer and the call throws TypeError; hand back something that is not a boolean and the return throws.

return also ends that call — everything after it in the body is skipped, which is how a function bails out early. A trailing parameter can carry a default value; defaults must come last in the list.

blocks.title: early return, and a default parameter
blocks.code:
<?php

function getDayName(int $day, string $fallback = 'Unknown day'): string
{
    if ($day === 1) {
        return 'Monday';
    }

    if ($day === 2) {
        return 'Tuesday';
    }

    return $fallback;
}

for ($i = 1; $i <= 3; $i++) {
    echo getDayName($i), "\n";
}

echo getDayName(9), "\n";
echo getDayName(9, 'No such day'), "\n";
blocks.output:
Monday
Tuesday
Unknown day
Unknown day
No such day

blocks.title: a nullable array, a void function, an int
blocks.code:
<?php

$students = [
    ['Student ID' => 1001, 'Student Name' => 'Juan Dela Cruz'],
    ['Student ID' => 1002, 'Student Name' => 'Maria Santos'],
];

// an array, or null when nothing matches
function findStudentById(array $students, int $id): ?array
{
    foreach ($students as $student) {
        if ($student['Student ID'] === $id) {
            return $student;
        }
    }

    return null;
}

// returns nothing at all: the printing is the whole job
function showStudent(?array $student): void
{
    if ($student === null) {
        echo 'Student Not Found', "\n";
        return;
    }

    echo $student['Student ID'], ' - ', $student['Student Name'], "\n";
}

function countStudents(array $students): int
{
    return count($students);
}

showStudent(findStudentById($students, 1002));
showStudent(findStudentById($students, 9999));
echo countStudents($students), ' students', "\n";
blocks.output:
1002 - Maria Santos
Student Not Found
2 students

blocks.html: ?array means an array or null: the question mark makes the type nullable, so return null; is legal there. : void means the function returns nothing; it exists for its side effect. This is why we write the types down — return nothing from a function declared : string and PHP throws a TypeError at that instant, not a wrong value three screens later.

blocks.title: the call comes first
blocks.code:
<?php

// The declaration is below the call, and this still works.
echo (isEven(4) ? 'four is even' : 'four is odd'), "\n";

function isEven(int $number): bool
{
    return $number % 2 === 0;
}

blocks.html: PHP compiles the whole file before it runs a single line, so an unconditional top-level function declaration is available everywhere in that file — even above the definition. Two limits: the declaration must not sit inside an if or inside another function, and it only helps in a file that has already been included.

blocks.title: a function body is its own scope
blocks.code:
<?php

$balance = 5000.00;

function seesBalance(): string
{
    // $balance exists out there, but a function body cannot see it.
    return isset($balance) ? 'yes' : 'no';
}

function withdrawFromGlobal(float $amount): float
{
    global $balance; // the explicit door to the outside

    return $balance - $amount;
}

echo 'can the function see $balance: ', seesBalance(), "\n";
echo 'with global: ', number_format(withdrawFromGlobal(1500), 2), "\n";
blocks.output:
can the function see $balance: no
with global: 3,500.00

blocks.html:
That is the surprise for everyone arriving from a language with file-wide locals: a function body is a separate scope. Outer variables are invisible unless you pass them in as parameters or import them with global. With neither, PHP treats the name as a fresh local and warns Warning: Undefined variable $balance.

Prefer parameters and return values. global works, but it hides the dependency: a reader cannot tell what the function touches from its signature.

blocks.title: arrow functions and closures
blocks.code:
<?php

$numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4];
$factor = 3;

$doubled = array_map(fn($x) => $x * 2, $numbers);
echo implode(', ', $doubled), "\n";

// fn captures $factor from the enclosing scope automatically
$scaled = array_map(fn($x) => $x * $factor, $numbers);
echo implode(', ', $scaled), "\n";

// an anonymous function has to say what it uses
$addFee = function (float $amount) use ($factor) {
    return $amount + $factor;
};

echo number_format($addFee(997.00), 2), "\n";

blocks.html:
fn($x) => $x * 2 is an arrow function: one expression, and the value of that expression is returned — no return, no braces. It captures the enclosing variables it mentions, by value, without being asked.

An anonymous function () does not do that. It sees nothing from the outside except what you list after use. Both capture by value: the closure keeps the value the variable had when it was defined.

quiz.q: What does the return type ?array promise?
options: Any array-like value, such as a string
quiz.why: A leading ? marks the type nullable, so both array and null are legal returns. Returning anything else throws a TypeError.

quiz.q: A function is declared at the top level of a file, below the line that calls it. What happens?
options: Fatal error: the function does not exist yet
The call works, because the file is compiled before it runs
It works only if the function has no parameters
quiz.why: Unconditional top-level declarations are hoisted, so they are callable anywhere in that file. A declaration inside an if or another function is not.

quiz.q: Inside a function, what does $total hold when $total was set just before the call?
options: Nothing: it is a fresh local unless passed in or declared global
A copy, but only for arrays
quiz.why: Each function body is its own scope. Reading an outer name without global gives a Warning: Undefined variable and null.

exercise.brief: Write a function discount(float $price, int $percent = 10): float that returns the price after removing percent. Then print two lines: discount(500) and discount(500, 25), each formatted with number_format($value, 2).
exercise.starter:
<?php

// declare discount(), then print the two formatted results
exercise.hint: The return value is $price - $price * $percent / 100. Echo with echo number_format(discount(500), 2), "\n";
exercise.solution:
<?php

function discount(float $price, int $percent = 10): float
{
    return $price - $price * $percent / 100;
}

echo number_format(discount(500), 2), "\n";
echo number_format(discount(500, 25), 2), "\n";
